name: poly_bevel_dirty_parity
description: Polygon bevel across its flag space -- inset only, shift only, both, grouped and ungrouped, two segments, square corners, a negative inset, a doubled application, and a star selection -- on dirty bases. The existing bevel fixtures are dump-oracles for single flags on clean cages; these cross the flags with the geometry.

provenance.notes: `nogroup` is the separating flag: with grouping off each selected face bevels alone, so the shared edges of a multi-face base come apart, and the two answers differ in vertex count as well as position. CHANNELS: the sweep's comparison was never vertex-only -- it compared the vertex multiset, the edge multiset, faces BOTH as ordered rings (winding shows) and as unordered position sets, the material partition, the per-face 'did this face's own tag change', and the post-command selection. Re-checked independently over all 215 frozen cases: ZERO agree on vertices while differing on ordered face rings, so nothing frozen here is a vertex-channel-only agreement. PRECISION: the sweep compared at 1e-4 and this fixture's tolerance matches it. The actual reproduction is far tighter -- 208 of the 215 cases are bit-identical at the dumps' 6 decimals and the remaining 7 agree to 3e-6 or better, that being the worst deviation anywhere in the set. The tolerance is the MEASUREMENT's bound, not the data's.
